title: Reading headlines
goal: Understand news headlines written in the nominal style and rewrite them as full sentences.

items.fr: augmenter → la hausse, fermer → la fermeture
items.en: turning verbs into nouns in headlines (nominal style)

drills.explain: The ending [[-ure]] makes a feminine noun: [[la fermeture]], like [[l'ouverture]].
de + les = [[des]]. Headlines drop many articles, but the little [[de]] that links the nouns stays.

drills.prompt: Which noun goes with the verb arrêter (the police arrest someone)?
options: l'arrestation
l'arrêtement
l'arrêtage

items.fr: Grève des chauffeurs → Les chauffeurs sont en grève.
items.en: rewriting a headline as a full sentence

drills.text: Grève des chauffeurs d'autobus → Les chauffeurs d'autobus sont ___ grève.
drills.en: Bus drivers' strike → The bus drivers are on strike.

options: Le chômage baisse à Halifax.
Le chômage augmente à Halifax.
Il n'y a pas de chômage à Halifax.
drills.explain: [[la baisse]] is the noun of [[baisser]] (to go down). [[le chômage]] = unemployment.

drills.prompt: Rewrite as a full sentence in the present: “Hausse des loyers à Montréal.”
accept: Les loyers sont en hausse à Montréal.
À Montréal, les loyers sont en hausse.
drills.explain: [[la hausse]] → the verb [[augmenter]]; the noun after [[de]] becomes the subject: [[les loyers augmentent]].

example.fr: La hausse des prix inquiète les familles.
example.en: The rise in prices worries families.

items.note: The h is “aspirated”: say and write [[la hausse]], never *l'hausse*. Synonym: [[l'augmentation]].

example.fr: Baisse du prix de l'essence en Ontario
Fermeture d'un pont à Laval pour travaux
example.en: Bridge closed in Laval for construction

example.fr: Ouverture d'une nouvelle bibliothèque à Moncton
Les infirmières sont en grève depuis lundi.
example.en: The nurses have been on strike since Monday.

items.note: [[être en grève]] = to be on strike. Don't confuse with [[grave]] (serious).

example.fr: Une manifestation pour le climat a eu lieu samedi à Montréal.
example.en: A climate protest took place on Saturday in Montréal.

items.note: Informal: [[une manif]]. The people are [[les manifestants]].

items.en: fire (a building or forest on fire)

example.fr: Un incendie a détruit un immeuble à Sherbrooke.
example.en: A fire destroyed a building in Sherbrooke.

items.note: [[un incendie]] is a dangerous fire; [[un feu]] can be any fire, even a campfire.

example.fr: Il y a des travaux sur l'autoroute tout l'été.
example.en: There's roadwork on the highway all summer.

example.fr: J'ai seulement lu les titres ce matin.
example.en: I only read the headlines this morning.

steps.title: Today's front page
steps.intro: Headlines are short, fast and full of nouns. Read these eight headlines from an online news site. Don't translate word for word: ask yourself **what happened, and where?**

blocks.title: Le Fil Info, Tuesday morning
blocks.context: The homepage of a (fictional) Canadian news site.
blocks.fr:
Hausse de 7 % des loyers à Montréal en un an
Grève des chauffeurs d'autobus à Gatineau : service réduit lundi
Fermeture d'un pont à Laval pour travaux tout l'été
Incendie dans un immeuble de Sherbrooke : aucun blessé
Ouverture d'une nouvelle bibliothèque à Moncton
Baisse du prix de l'essence en Ontario
Tempête de neige : écoles fermées à Québec mardi
Un cycliste blessé au centre-ville de Vancouver
blocks.en: Rents up 7% in a year in Montréal. Bus drivers' strike in Gatineau: reduced service on Monday. Bridge closed in Laval for roadwork all summer. Fire in a Sherbrooke apartment building: nobody injured. New library opens in Moncton. Gas prices drop in Ontario. Snowstorm: schools closed in Québec City on Tuesday. Cyclist injured in downtown Vancouver.

blocks.prompt: What does the first headline tell you?
options: Rents in Montréal went up by 7% in a year.
7% of Montrealers rent their home.
Rents in Montréal went down by 7%.
blocks.explain: [[la hausse]] = the rise. [[Hausse des loyers]] → [[Les loyers ont augmenté]].

blocks.prompt: Which headline is about workers who stopped working?
options: Grève des chauffeurs d'autobus à Gatineau
Fermeture d'un pont à Laval
Ouverture d'une nouvelle bibliothèque à Moncton
blocks.explain: [[une grève]] = a strike. The drivers are [[en grève]], so there are fewer buses.

blocks.prompt: “Un cycliste blessé au centre-ville de Vancouver”: what's missing compared with a normal sentence?
options: The auxiliary verb (a été)
The subject
The place
blocks.explain: A full sentence would be [[Un cycliste a été blessé au centre-ville de Vancouver.]] Headlines often keep only the past participle.

blocks.title: The nominal style
blocks.body:
A normal sentence is built around a **verb**: [[Les loyers augmentent à Montréal.]] A headline is often built around a **noun** made from that verb: [[Hausse des loyers à Montréal.]] This is called the **nominal style** (*style nominal*).

The recipe is almost always the same:

- **the action as a noun**: [[hausse, fermeture, grève, ouverture]]
- **+ de + who or what**: [[des loyers]], [[d'un pont]], [[des chauffeurs]]
- **+ where or when**: [[à Montréal]], [[mardi]]
- **+ a colon for the key detail**: [[: aucun blessé]], [[: service réduit lundi]]

To understand a headline, **put the verb back**. Ask: which verb is hiding in this noun? Who does it?

blocks.title: From verb to noun
head: Verb
Noun
Ending and gender
blocks.note: A safe rule of thumb: nouns in **-tion** and **-ure** are feminine; nouns in **-ment** and **-age** are masculine. [[licencier]] = to lay off; [[déneiger]] = to clear snow.

blocks.title: Putting the verb back
blocks.pattern: Nom + de + qui / quoi + où → Qui / quoi + verbe + où
blocks.note: The noun after [[de]] usually becomes the **subject** of the sentence. Use the present for news that is happening now, the passé composé for news that is finished.

examples.fr: Hausse des loyers à Montréal → Les loyers augmentent à Montréal.
examples.en: Rise in rents in Montréal → Rents are going up in Montréal.

examples.fr: Grève des chauffeurs à Gatineau → Les chauffeurs sont en grève à Gatineau.
examples.en: Drivers' strike in Gatineau → The drivers are on strike in Gatineau.

examples.fr: Ouverture d'une bibliothèque à Moncton → Une nouvelle bibliothèque ouvre à Moncton.
examples.en: Opening of a library in Moncton → A new library is opening in Moncton.

examples.fr: Arrestation de deux suspects à Laval → La police a arrêté deux suspects à Laval.
examples.en: Arrest of two suspects in Laval → Police arrested two suspects in Laval.

blocks.title: Other headline tricks
head: Trick
Headline
Full sentence
rows: Un cycliste a été blessé à Vancouver.
Le maire de Sherbrooke a démissionné.
À cause de la tempête, les écoles sont fermées.
« Nous sommes inquiets », disent les locataires
Les locataires disent qu'ils sont inquiets.
Vers une hausse des tarifs du métro
Les tarifs du métro vont probablement augmenter.
Est-ce que le télétravail est une bonne idée ?
blocks.note: [[démissionner]] = to resign; [[les locataires]] = tenants; [[les tarifs]] = fares, rates. Notice the reported speech in the quotation line: you learned it in unit 2.

blocks.title: Traps in headlines
blocks.body:
- **False friends:** [[une manifestation]] is a protest, not a “manifestation”. [[les travaux]] are roadwork or construction, not “works”. [[un incendie]] is a fire, not an incident.
- **Look-alikes:** [[la grève]] (strike) ≠ [[grave]] (serious). [[la baisse]] (drop) ≠ [[basse]] (low).
- **No élision with hausse:** the h of [[hausse]] is aspirated, so it's [[la hausse]] and [[une forte hausse]], never *l'hausse*.
- **Keep the contractions:** [[Hausse de les loyers]] is wrong → [[Hausse des loyers]]. [[Baisse de le prix]] → [[Baisse du prix]].
- **Noun or adjective?** [[Fermeture d'un pont]] (the closure of a bridge, noun) vs [[Pont fermé]] (bridge closed, past participle). Both are possible headlines; they mean almost the same thing.

blocks.title: Why do journalists write like this?
blocks.body:
Space and speed. A noun says in one word what a sentence says in four: [[Fermeture]] = *they are going to close it / it is closed*. It also sounds **neutral and objective**, because there's no subject saying *who* decided.

That's also why headlines can be vague. [[Hausse des tarifs]] does not tell you who raised the fares or when. The first lines of the article (the *chapeau*) give you those details. In the next lesson you'll read whole articles.

blocks.title: Headlines in Québec and Canada
blocks.body:
Some words you'll see often in Canadian French headlines:

- [[fin de semaine]] for *weekend* (Québec usage; France says [[week-end]]): [[Travaux sur le pont toute la fin de semaine]].
- [[le déneigement]] (snow removal) and [[une tempête]]: winter news is everywhere from November to March.
- [[les nids-de-poule]] (potholes): used everywhere, but a classic spring headline in Montréal.
- [[la mairesse]] for a female mayor, very common in Québec; France usually says [[la maire]].
- [[l'autobus]] or [[le bus]], and [[l'essence]] for gas (in casual Québec speech you'll hear *le gaz*, but news writing says [[l'essence]]).

blocks.title: Read like a news anchor
blocks.note: News anchors read headlines with a clear, falling tone and a short pause at the colon.

lines.tip: la hausse: no link, no élision. Say [os], like “oss”.

lines.fr: Grève des chauffeurs d'autobus à Gatineau.
Fermeture d'un pont à Laval pour travaux.
lines.en: Bridge closed in Laval for roadwork.
lines.tip: fer-meu-ture: the middle e is light or almost silent.

lines.fr: Incendie dans un immeuble de Sherbrooke : aucun blessé.
lines.en: Fire in a Sherbrooke building: nobody injured.
lines.tip: Pause at the colon, then lower your voice for the detail.

lines.fr: Ouverture d'une nouvelle bibliothèque à Moncton.
Baisse du prix de l'essence en Ontario.
lines.tip: baisse [bɛs] has an s sound; basse [bas] is a different word.

blocks.fr: Fermeture de la ligne verte du métro dimanche.
blocks.en: Green metro line closed on Sunday.
options: A metro line will be closed.
A new metro line will open.
The metro will be free.
blocks.explain: [[la fermeture]] = the closure. The opposite would be [[l'ouverture]].

options: Fewer people are unemployed in New Brunswick.
More people are unemployed in New Brunswick.
There's a strike in New Brunswick.
blocks.explain: [[la baisse]] = the drop. [[le chômage]] = unemployment. So [[le chômage baisse]].

steps.title: Your turn
steps.intro: Decode headlines and write your own. Remember: put the verb back, or take the verb out.

blocks.en: Prices are going up. → Rise in prices

blocks.prompt: Match each verb with its noun.

options: Nurses are on strike in Québec City.
Nurses are in a serious situation in Québec City.
Québec City is hiring nurses.
A nurse was injured in Québec City.
optionFeedback: Hiring would be embauche or recrutement.

blocks.prompt: Write the headline in French: “Closure of a bridge in Laval”
accept: Fermeture d'un pont à Laval pour travaux
blocks.explain: Nominal style: [[Fermeture]] + [[d'un pont]] + [[à Laval]]. No verb, no article at the start.

blocks.en: Rise in the price of gas in Ontario
blocks.explain: de + le = [[du]] ([[le prix]]); [[essence]] starts with a vowel → [[de l']].

blocks.prompt: The police arrested two men in Laval. Which is the best headline?
options: Arrestation de deux hommes à Laval
Arrêter deux hommes à Laval
Deux hommes arrestation à Laval
blocks.explain: The headline uses the **noun** [[arrestation]] + [[de]] + who + where. The infinitive [[arrêter]] would sound like an instruction.

blocks.prompt: Rewrite as a full sentence in the present: “Grève des chauffeurs d'autobus à Gatineau.”
accept: Les chauffeurs d'autobus sont en grève à Gatineau.
À Gatineau, les chauffeurs d'autobus sont en grève.
Les chauffeurs d'autobus font la grève à Gatineau.
Les chauffeurs d'autobus font grève à Gatineau.
Les chauffeurs de bus sont en grève à Gatineau.
À Gatineau, les chauffeurs d'autobus font grève.
blocks.explain: [[être en grève]] or [[faire grève]] = to be on strike. The noun after [[de]] ([[les chauffeurs]]) becomes the subject.

blocks.prompt: Gas prices drop in Ontario (as a headline).
accept: Baisse du prix de l'essence en Ontario
blocks.explain: Noun first ([[Baisse]]), then [[du prix de l'essence]], then the place.

blocks.fr: Ouverture d'une nouvelle bibliothèque à Moncton.
blocks.explain: [[ouverture]] comes from [[ouvrir]]; [[bibliothèque]] has an è and ends in -thèque.

blocks.text: Le maire ___ démissionné hier. Le titre : « Le maire démissionne ».
blocks.en: The mayor resigned yesterday. The headline: “Mayor resigns”.
blocks.explain: [[démissionner]] takes avoir: [[il a démissionné]]. Headlines often use the present for a recent past event.

blocks.prompt: Write four headlines in the nominal style about real or invented news in your city: something going up or down, a closure or an opening, a strike or a protest, and the weather. Then rewrite one of them as a full sentence.
blocks.promptFr: Écrivez quatre titres sur l'actualité de votre ville, puis récrivez un titre en phrase complète.
checklist: Four headlines that start with a noun (hausse, baisse, fermeture, grève…)
de / du / des after the noun
A place in each headline (à + city)
One headline with a colon and a detail
One headline rewritten as a full sentence with a verb

models.label: Model answer
models.fr:
Hausse du prix du transport en commun à Ottawa
Fermeture de la piscine municipale pour travaux
Manifestation des étudiants devant le Parlement
Tempête de neige : vols annulés à l'aéroport

Phrase complète : Le prix du transport en commun augmente à Ottawa.
models.en: Public transit fares up in Ottawa. Municipal pool closed for repairs. Student protest in front of Parliament. Snowstorm: flights cancelled at the airport. Full sentence: Public transit fares are going up in Ottawa.

blocks.prompt: A friend asks: « Quoi de neuf dans les nouvelles ? » Read three headlines from Le Fil Info, then explain each one in a full sentence in your own words.
checklist: Explain each one with a verb (augmenter, être en grève, ouvrir…)
Add a short reaction (C'est une bonne nouvelle ! / C'est inquiétant.)

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Alors, il y a « Hausse de 7 % des loyers à Montréal ». Ça veut dire que les loyers ont augmenté de 7 % en un an. C'est inquiétant ! Ensuite, « Grève des chauffeurs d'autobus à Gatineau » : les chauffeurs sont en grève, donc il y a moins d'autobus lundi. Et enfin, une bonne nouvelle : une nouvelle bibliothèque ouvre à Moncton.
models.en: So, there's “Rents up 7% in Montréal”. That means rents went up 7% in a year. That's worrying! Next, “Bus drivers' strike in Gatineau”: the drivers are on strike, so there are fewer buses on Monday. And finally, some good news: a new library is opening in Moncton.

summary:
- Recognize the **nominal style** of headlines: [[Hausse des loyers à Montréal]]
- Turn verbs into nouns and back: [[fermer → la fermeture]], [[augmenter → la hausse]]
- Rewrite a headline as a full sentence and spot false friends like [[manifestation]] and [[grève]]
